title: Carry-on only packing list: fit the actual limit
dek: Start with your fare's bag allowance, then pack essentials, a realistic clothing rotation and a removable pouch for any forced gate check.
metaDescription: Start with your fare's bag allowance, then pack essentials, a realistic clothing rotation and a removable pouch for any forced gate check.

paragraphs: To pack carry-on only, confirm the allowance for every flight on your itinerary, choose a bag within the applicable dimensions and weight, then pack essential items before clothes. Plan laundry if your quantities depend on it. Keep a removable set of documents, medicines and restricted batteries in case the main bag must be checked at the gate.

A bag sold as cabin size is not a promise that your fare includes it or that every operator accepts it. The practical challenge is meeting the actual allowance while retaining access to what cannot go in the hold. This guide uses US security and battery sources; other departure airports and airlines may have different or stricter rules.

body.heading: Check the allowance before the packing list
items: Open the current baggage terms for your fare and each operating airline. Distinguish an under-seat personal item from an overhead cabin bag.
Measure the bag as required, including wheels, handles and any packed expansion. Weigh the packed bag rather than relying on its empty specification.
Identify essential medicines, aids, documents and devices before deciding how much space clothes can use. Ask the airline about special equipment where needed.
Choose clothing for the actual conditions and a realistic laundry plan. Use a small rotation rather than assuming every possible activity needs another outfit.
Separate ordinary liquids from items needing a specific exemption or screening arrangement. Check unusual items with the responsible authority.
Pack a removable essentials pouch and battery-safe arrangement. Review it again if staff require a gate check.

body.heading: Example: a week with confirmed laundry
rows: Tops
Four
A mix of rewear and one planned wash.
Bottoms
Two
One worn and one packed.
Underwear and socks
Five sets
Confirmed wash and drying before supplies run out.
Layer
One
Suited to the forecast and worn where useful.
Shoes
One worn pair; second only for a real need
Footwear is bulky and must justify its space.

body.heading: The example is not a universal capsule wardrobe
paragraphs: These are invented choices for one adult in mild conditions. They are not suitable for every body, climate, medical need or activity. If laundry cannot be confirmed, revise the quantities or baggage plan. Do not create an unrealistic wash schedule merely to make the bag close.

Compression can reduce clothing volume but not weight. Leave enough space to close the bag normally and move through the trip without repacking every pocket at each stop. If required items exceed the allowance, change the baggage arrangement rather than hiding weight or risking loss of necessary supplies.

body.heading: Liquids and batteries need different checks
paragraphs: The [TSA checklist](https://www.tsa.gov/sites/default/files/tsa-travel-checklist.pdf) gives the ordinary US carry-on liquids rule: containers no larger than 3.4 ounces in one quart-size bag per passenger. Exceptions require their own check. Decanting is not appropriate for every medicine or product, and a small container does not establish that the destination permits the substance.

The [FAA battery guidance](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries) treats power banks and spare lithium batteries as carry-on only. Installed batteries have different rules. Protect the relevant terminals, check ratings and ask the airline about stricter limits or specialist equipment. Do not generalize "all electronics are forbidden in checked bags."

body.heading: If the main bag is gate checked
rows: Travel documents, payment method and valuables
They are not trapped in the checked bag.
Required medicines and essential aids
You retain needed access and follow relevant restrictions.
Power banks and spare lithium batteries
Remove them from the bag going into the hold.
Arrival information and a suitable spare outfit
You can manage if baggage delivery is delayed.

body.heading: Example: the gate-check fallback
paragraphs: Invented example: a traveler meets the airline's size limit but staff need the bag in the hold. The traveler removes the essentials pouch and power bank before handing it over, asks where the bag will be returned and keeps the tag. This is a contingency, not a prediction that compliant luggage is always guaranteed cabin space.

Do not assume a tiny personal item can hold everything you need to remove. Test the fallback at home, especially with assistive equipment or temperature-sensitive supplies. Ask the airline and relevant professional about those needs in advance rather than improvising at boarding.

body.heading: Make the last edit about usefulness
paragraphs: Remove duplication before removing essentials: extra chargers that do the same job, shoes with no planned use or clothing that does not suit the forecast. Keep the [week-away list](/guides/packing-list-for-a-week-away) for the personal-versus-shared distinction.

If your itinerary changes, review the baggage rules again, including any replacement flight. A new operator or fare can change the allowance. Stop and contact the airline where equipment, batteries or required supplies do not clearly fit its rules.

items.q: Does carry-on only mean one bag on every fare?
items.a: No. The phrase describes your plan, not an included allowance. Some fares permit only an under-seat item, while others include an overhead bag under particular limits. Check your actual booking and operating airlines before choosing the bag or assuming a second item is included.

items.q: Can I bring a power bank?
items.a: Check its rating and the airline's current restrictions. FAA guidance requires power banks and spare lithium batteries to remain in the cabin, not checked baggage. If the bag is gate checked, remove them first. Larger, damaged, recalled or specialist batteries need their own assessment rather than a generic yes.

items.q: Can I pack for two weeks without a checked bag?
items.a: Possibly, if essential equipment, climate and a dependable laundry plan fit the actual allowance. The clothing rotation may be similar to a shorter trip, but washing and drying become important dependencies. Do not treat carry-on travel as a requirement when checked baggage is the practical choice.
